javaWebIntegration.receipt: Native lifecycle=destroyed plus web.lifecycle=detached, web.storage=webkit-managed and host/guest-stop web.saveStage=prepared; explicit unused when no WebKit data store was opened. Failed preparation remains sticky through final detach.
javaWebIntegration.legacyPolicy: Existing native data without a marker retains the old package UUID. Clearing that save drops its binding and uses a fresh UUID on next launch; shared legacy WebKit bytes are retained to protect other libraries.
remaining: Real HTTP application/third-party plugin persistence; post-didCommit asynchronous history-restoration checks racing host stop; broader Activity replacement/recreate ordering; page-script direct file URLs; file subframe remapping; loading documents. Cross-origin child frame saving is unsupported and fails closed. Synthetic lifecycle has isTrusted=false; event.waitUntil is a Husk extension. Unregistered asynchronous work and trusted browser unload are not guaranteed. Saved non-GET history requires explicit application recovery.
Generic Thread.interrupt and blocking-wait semantics, macOS 14 hardware, WebKit process failure recovery and network-cancellation timeouts remain unverified.
javaWebIntegration.saveStage: Host-requested close or final Activity guest finish keeps Java bridge dispatch alive, suspends media, blocks new navigation and ordinary recurring tasks, delivers synthetic lifecycle once, awaits event.waitUntil promises and same-origin child frames within six seconds, then drains immediate AppMain messages before Android destruction. Later actual unload is gated; late bridge calls and all observed save failures reject storage-closed.
javaWebIntegration.guestFinish: Opt-in AppMain callback defers final Activity/whole-stack affinity destruction to host saving and existing phase 10 teardown. Recheck after already-queued launches; preserve child results, deduplicate requests and reject Activity launches/recreate after handoff. NULL callback keeps old host behavior. Process.killProcess still fails lifecycle acknowledgement. A valid stopping event starts the existing 30-second deadline without heartbeat extensions.
javaWebIntegration.perViewDestroy: Direct WebView.destroy closes normal APIs but retains Java plugin/resource dispatch until a bounded save, JavaBridge/AppMain acknowledgement and WebKit detach. Other views continue. Whole-session preparation waits retiring views; all observed failures stay sticky. AndroidX listeners execute on AppMain before reply, and ReplyProxy can reply during preparation. Empty detach documents do not rerun application user scripts.
javaWebIntegration.navigation: App-initiated loadUrl and allowed main-frame navigation wait for the prior document save. WebViewClient policy runs before irreversible saving; vetoes, custom URLs and same-document fragments preserve the live document. Save timeouts/callbacks belong to a document generation; caught Java plugin errors cancel navigation and fail final storage acknowledgement. Confirmed sealed GET history documents reload in their original list position without duplicate lifecycle; ordinary history loads are not repeated. Saved non-GET history is rejected before leaving the current page, without automatic POST resubmission. Unsupported file subframe remaps are rejected instead of replacing the main page. Nine packaged DEX navigation tests and the full suite pass. Host stop during navigation preparation joins the existing save, cancels the pending decision immediately and preserves its six-second deadline; success, rejection and a late-stop timeout are covered by real loopback HTTP DEX tests.
javaWebIntegration.httpValidation: Six packaged real-DEX tests use a disposable loopback HTTP server: async save POST, redirect/history request counts, localStorage/IndexedDB/Java plugin process reopen, persisted outgoing cookie, HttpOnly visibility, stop/save overlap, and an admitted but uncommitted history response released after host stop. The last case rejects new page commits and duplicate saves/requests, then reopens both Web stores and Java state. Post-didCommit asynchronous history-restoration checks racing stop remain open. Controlled-fixture evidence, not third-party HTTP application compatibility.

navigationDestroyValidation.evidence: Real DEX/WebKit sessions overlap pending navigation saving with per-view destroy. Destination never starts or commits; lifecycle is delivered once; the replacement view runs; Java plugin and queued UI writes drain. Successful localStorage/IndexedDB/Java state is read back after independent process reopen. Failures never emit storage-closed. A late destroy plus host stop preserves the original six-second deadline. Existing production implementation passed without a runtime patch.
